reason: Both correctly reassured the homeowner that pan-dependent buzzing is normal and neither pushed an unsupported part or repair, but Conversation 2 nailed the hidden truth directly, naming multi-layer sandwich bases as the cause, explaining fan run-on as normal, and giving a precise 'when to worry' list (rattling or grinding, codes, noise with every pan, cracked glass) that covered the important unknowns in one efficient reply. Conversation 1 reached the right conclusion through sensible questions, but its second reply contained a garbled sentence ('Burning smells, or cracking sounds, your hob is fine') that reads as the opposite of a safety boundary, recommended a silicone mat under a stockpot on high power, which is questionable advice for an induction surface, and padded both turns with an irrelevant tripping-electrics safety panel. Conversation 2's single, accurate, well-bounded answer served the homeowner better.
